name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
principle: Externally influenced data is allowed to reach template source or template syntax without proper neutralization. The engine then interprets attacker-controlled template directives or expressions as code, enabling injection and possible code execution.
detection_signals: Template source is built from request/query/header/body data, then passed to a template parser/compiler, e.g. `Template(userInput)`, `createTemplate(userInput)`, `renderString(userInput)`.
Template syntax markers are concatenated with untrusted data before rendering, e.g. `"{{" + x + "}}"`, `${x}`, `<%` + x + `%>`.
Dynamic template name/path comes from user input, e.g. `loadTemplate(req.getParameter(...))`, `include(param)`, `extends(param)` without allowlist.
Untrusted text is passed to engine eval/parse/compile APIs instead of as a model variable, e.g. `evalTemplate(...)`, `compileTemplate(...)`, `processString(...)`.
Template engine is instantiated with unrestricted defaults while accepting user-controlled template text, e.g. no sandbox/restricted mode or unsafe resolver/class access settings.
User input is read from a source and later becomes the first argument to render/process methods, not a model map entry.
negative_signals: Template is a fixed literal or bundled resource, and only data values are bound into the context, e.g. `render(FIXED_TEMPLATE, model)`.
User input is added only to a variable map/context, e.g. `model.put("name", request.getParameter(...))`, with no template parsing of that value.
Sandbox/restricted mode is enabled, e.g. `SandboxedEnvironment`, `setNewBuiltinClassResolver(TemplateClassResolver.ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER)`, or equivalent locked-down configuration.
Template names are selected from a constant enum/allowlist before lookup, not from raw user input.
No string concatenation/interpolation is used to construct template syntax delimiters or directives.
The engine renders precompiled templates from trusted sources only, with user data treated as escaped output values.
false_defense_traps: HTML escaping the user input before inserting it into template source; escaping does not stop template expression parsing.
Regex stripping a few tokens such as `{{`, `${`, or `<%`; alternate delimiters, filters, or nested expressions can still work.
Blacklisting `eval` while still calling template compile/parse on attacker-controlled text.
Sanitizing output after rendering; the injection already occurred during template evaluation.
verification_focus: Can any attacker-controlled value reach the template source or expression parser, instead of only the template context data?

consequence_chains.trigger: attacker controls template text or directives that the engine interprets
consequence_chains.consequence: arbitrary code or command execution through template expression evaluation

consequence_chains.trigger: template injection is reflected into browser-visible output
consequence_chains.consequence: cross-site scripting and client-side script execution

patch_principle: Keep template source fixed and trusted; pass untrusted values only as data bindings.
Enable sandbox/restricted mode and disable dangerous expression access, function calls, and class loading.
Allowlist template identifiers and reject raw user-supplied template text.
Precompile templates from trusted resources; never compile or evaluate user-provided template strings.
